FT "美 제재 피한 3단계 밀수망…中 게임사·페이퍼컴퍼니·프린스그룹 얽혀" 사진=AFP 미국의 수출 통제를 피해 엔비디아의 인공지능(AI) 반도체를 중국으로 들여보낸 우회 공급망에 중국 게임업계와 역외 페이퍼컴퍼니는 물론 캄보디아 기반 범죄조직까지 얽혀 있다는 외신 보도가 나왔다. 젠슨 황 전 엔비디아 최고경영자(CEO)와 사적 관계였던 중국인 여성 사업가 앨리스 황(중국명 황러)이 이 네트워크의 핵심 연결고리로 지목됐다. 21일(현지시간) 영국 파이낸셜타임스(FT)는 소식통 10여 명과 수백 건의 기업 공시 자료를 분석한 결과, 엔비디아 칩이 중국 암시장으로 유입되는 과정이 △반도체 구매·공급이 허용된 업체 △미국 수출 통제 대상에서 벗어난 고객사 △물품 밀반입과 자금 세탁을 맡는 지하조직 등 3개 경로로 구성됐다고 보도했다. 앞서 미국 IT 전문매체 디인포메이션은 앨리스 황이 젠슨 황과의 관계를 이용해 최소 75억달러(약 10조원) 규모의 미국산 AI 칩을 중국에 우회 공급했다는 의혹을 제기한 바 있다. FT에 따르면 미국 내 조달 창구 역할을 한 곳은 엔비디아의 주요 중국 협력사인 인스퍼의 미국 계열사 '에이브러스'다. 인스퍼는 2023년 3월 미국 제재 명단에 올랐으나, 인스퍼가 일부 지분을 보유한 에이브러스는 제재를 피해 주문자상표부착생산(OEM) 파트너로 엔비디아와 거래를 이어갔다. 엔비디아 칩을 대량 구매하려면 경영진과 사주 과반이 중국인이 아니라는 최소 3년 치 증빙이 필요하다. 인스퍼의 중국 고객들은 이 요건을 맞추기 위해 중국 온라인 게임사 '센추리 화퉁'의 도움을 받아 싱가포르 기반 데이터센터 업체 '메가스피드'를 활용했다고 소식통들은 전했다. 메가스피드는 중국 게임사 '세븐로드'의 싱가포르 법인이 2023년 사명을 바꾼 회사로, 앨리스 황이 대외 임원을 맡았다. 앨리스 황의 남편 캉웨이는 센추리 화퉁의 초기 투자자이자 2020년 센추리 화퉁과 함께 세븐로드에 투자한 인물이다. 실제 대규모 물량 이동도 확인됐다. 2024년 12월부터 1년간 메가스피드의 말레이시아 계열사 스피드매트릭스가 에이브러스로부터 수입한 물량은 신고액 기준 46억달러(약 6조2000억원)에 달한다. 소식통들은 이 칩의 상당수가 동남아 밀수 경로를 거쳐 중국 암시장으로 흘러 들어가 원래 가격의 몇 배에 거래됐으며, 앨리스 황 측과 센추리 화퉁이 합작해 세운 '상하이 센추리 리퉁'이 중국 내 주요 유통업체 중 하나였다고 밝혔다. 밀반입과 자금 세탁을 담당한 지하조직으로는 캄보디아를 거점으로 온라인 사기와 돈세탁을 벌여온 '프린스그룹'이 지목됐다. 프린스그룹은 한국인 납치·감금 사건이 발생한 캄보디아 '태자단지'의 배후로도 알려진 조직이다. 미 당국의 제재 대상에 오른 뒤 지난 6월 일본에서 체포된 프린스그룹 2인자 후샤오웨이가 온라인 게임 사업의 지분 관계와 지식재산권(IP) 협력을 매개로 센추리 화퉁과 연결돼 칩 밀수에 관여했다는 것이 소식통들의 설명이다. FT는 온라인 게임이 게임머니와 아이템을 통한 자금 세탁에 자주 악용되는 데다, AI 붐 이전까지 게임과 암호화폐 업계가 중국 내 엔비디아 그래픽처리장치(GPU)의 최대 수요처였다는 점이 게임업계와 범죄조직의 결합 배경이 됐다고 분석했다. 크리스 클라그 국제전략문제연구소(IISS) 연구원은 FT에 "칩 밀수는 공급망 구조 측면에서 마약이나 무기 밀수와

items.fullText: Ian Buck Kicks Off NVIDIA’s Week at SC26 as Science Enters the Age of Agents At SC26, NVIDIA’s VP of Hyperscale and HPC laid out how researchers can combine simulation, AI and agents to accelerate scientific discovery. November 17, 2026 by Brian Caulfield 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! NVIDIA’s Ian Buck kicked off the company’s week at SC26 in Chicago on Monday with new tools for AI agents, software that can plan experiments, run code and check results on researchers’ own systems. In NVIDIA’s special address, Buck announced Nemotron for Science , the Rubin HPC GPU and an expanded Vera CPU platform for high-performance computing . He also detailed a new collaboration in quantum computing with IBM and Fermi National Accelerator Laboratory . “The frontier of computing and the new scientific stack is going to be simulation, as always, but combined with AI and the future of quantum,” said Buck, vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing at NVIDIA. Buck opened the talk by looking back to his first public talk on CUDA, at an SC06 tutorial in Tampa, Florida, 20 years ago. NVIDIA now offers more than 1,000 CUDA-X libraries , he said. Open Models for Science Agents “[Agents] have been just a game changer in how we interface with our supercomputers, with our devices, our instruments and how we can do the research,” Buck said. Simulation remains the foundation of scientific computing, “which will always be on the top,” Buck said, with AI, quantum and now agents working alongside it. Nemotron for Science combines the Nemotron 3.5 Super VL open model with a new open chemistry dataset and post-training recipes for life sciences and chemistry, Buck explained. Researchers can run it locally on a DGX Spark, a workstation or their own supercomputer. items.fullText: Lambda Boosts AI Factory Resiliency and Efficiency With NVIDIA Photonics November 16, 2026 by Brian Sparks 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! To train an AI model, thousands of GPUs have to work together, requiring a network that’s fast, efficient and resilient. Lambda is tackling the network piece of the puzzle with NVIDIA Photonics co-packaged optics (CPO) switches. The cloud provider is using the switches to connect NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 racks with more than 10,000 GPUs, delivering lower power, higher resiliency and longer mean time between interruptions (MTBI) to an AI factory at scale. “Networking has to keep pace with the demands of increasingly large AI clusters,” said Dave Ward, president of cloud services at Lambda. “Bringing co-packaged optics into a deployment of this scale is an important step toward building the infrastructure needed to support the next generation of AI.” Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 In the company’s tests using the switches, network latency — the time needed for moving data — dropped by about 4% at rack scale and by up to about 10% at pod scale. Across rack, scalable unit and pod configurations, the network maintains the same throughput as conventional pluggable optics. Delivering Power Efficiency and Resiliency at Scale Improving power efficiency and resiliency matters because the network sits at the center of AI factory productivity. In a large training job, one interrupted link can stall thousands of GPUs. With agentic inference, one network disruption can introduce cascading latency effects on many agents. Every interruption costs time, and every watt spent on networking is a watt not available for compute. NVIDIA Photonics addresses both power efficiency and resiliency. By replacing pluggable transceivers with co-packaged optical engines on the switch package, it delivers up to 5x better power efficiency and up to 15x higher reliability than conventional pluggable optics. items.fullText: CUDA at 20: How the Platform Transformed Scientific Computing Over two decades, CUDA, the platform that turned GPUs into the engine of modern science, has advanced Nobel Prize-winning research and more. November 16, 2026 by Brett Murray 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! This week at SC26, NVIDIA is marking two decades of CUDA by honoring the researchers, developers and engineers who helped make GPU computing a foundation for modern science and AI. CUDA’s 20th anniversary presents an occasion to reflect across computing eras, from the people who wrote the very first CUDA programs to the AI developers building on their work today. At the platform’s core is this developer community whose experiments, tools and persistence expanded what accelerated computing could do. From SC06 to SC26 NVIDIA announced CUDA in November 2006 and brought it to the scientific community at SC06, giving scientists and developers a familiar, high-level programming model for using GPUs. It fundamentally extended accelerated computing beyond graphics use cases to accelerate demanding applications for science, simulation and more. In the two decades since, developers have used CUDA to advance Nobel Prize-winning AI research , accelerate scientific applications on supercomputers and support visual effects in Oscar-winning films . Today, more than 11 million developers build on CUDA across the computing stack. items.fullText: NVIDIA Announces Rubin HPC — A New GPU to Accelerate Agents for Science, Engineering and Analytics A record leap in CUDA cores with accelerated data movement shorten time to results for science and engineering workloads. November 16, 2026 by Dan Ernst 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Announced today at SC26, NVIDIA Rubin HPC is a new GPU in the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform designed to accelerate simulation and data processing for science, engineering and analytics workflows. As agents help scientists and engineers explore more candidate materials, molecules and designs, they rely on simulations to test those ideas and guide their next steps. Rubin HPC will accelerate those simulations, shortening the path from exploration to scientific discovery and industrial design. The Rubin HPC GPU features a record number of CUDA cores — more than 50,000 on a single GPU — as well as a sparse data acceleration capability that keeps those cores fed with data, and accelerates GPU-to-GPU connectivity with seventh-generation NVIDIA NVLink interconnect technology. Read All NVIDIA Announcements From SC26 Scientists and engineers rely on simulation to understand complex systems before committing to experiments or physical prototypes. Working with agents, these teams can explore more candidate materials, molecules and designs. This increases demand for the GPU-accelerated simulations needed to evaluate those ideas and guide next steps. “For agents tackling science and engineering, faster simulation means faster discovery,” said Ian Buck , vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing at NVIDIA. “Rubin HPC accelerates the simulations agents use to test ideas and guide their next steps, helping scientists and engineers explore more possibilities and bring breakthroughs closer.” Turning Faster Computation Into Faster Discovery Across climate models, engineering simulations, genomic analysis and financial risk, scientific computing w
